newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Monday in quiet trading as investors awaited the Bank of Israel announcement on interest rates, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.99 percent, or 2.56 points, to 260.47 on low all-share turnover of 137 million shekels against 173 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.08 percent higher at 269.67.
After the closing of trading the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for March by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 13.9 percent.

"The market was recovering today from Sunday's hysteria. There was no reason for yesterday's sharp decline -- investors were simply overreacting," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

The Mishtanim index plunged 3.23 percent on Sunday as the market reacted to news over the weekend that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had been cautioned by police that statements he made to them could be used against him in court, a procedure used by police when they believe charges may be filed.

Netanyahu was questioned last week in connection with charges that the short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general was part of a deal for a plea bargain in the corruption trial of Aryeh Deri, a key figure in the governing coalition.
"Everything depends now on the political situation. If the government falls the market will crash. If nothing happens the positive trend will continue," said Yosi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.
"Most investors were sitting on the fence today waiting to see what would happen with the interest rates. This can be seen by the fact the activity was relatively low today," Tsur said.

Tsur added that the market was becoming more selective. "The market is responding to the release of the first (fourth-quarter) earnings reports. The companies that released bad results were down today," he said.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most volume leader, fell 1.0 percent to 19,820 agorot on volume of 9.8 million shekels. Teva said on Monday that earnings per share rose in the fourth-quarter of 1996 to $0.49 from $0.31 at the same period in 1995.
"At first glance the results were above estimates, but Israeli investors are waiting for the reaction in New York," Tsur said.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 33,358 agorot on turnover of five million shekels, and Bank Leumi, which gained 1.25 percent to 570 agorot on volume of 3.9 million shekels.
